# Results — Study 326 (Stablecoin-Depeg) on real BTC/ETH daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). An **event study** of the
crypto basket (equal-weight BTC-USD + ETH-USD daily, Yahoo) around the two market-wide
stablecoin depegs — the **UST/Luna** algorithmic death spiral (2022-05-09) and the
**USDC** SVB-weekend break to $0.88 (2023-03-11). Cumulative abnormal return (CAR) over a
[-5, +10] trading-day window, benchmarked against a **synthetic control** of randomly-placed
non-event windows on the same tape. As-of **2026-05-31** (the in-progress month is dropped);
match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same data.*

## Data stamp

| Tape | Window | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| Basket (EW BTC+ETH ret) | 2017-01-02 → 2026-05-31 | 3,437 | `78f6589cd966` |
| BTC-USD | 2017-01-01 → 2026-05-31 | 3,438 | `16fc974afa4c` |
| ETH-USD | 2017-11-09 → 2026-05-31 | 3,126 | `4fb8ba51182c` |

## The headline — the two depegs point in opposite directions

| Event | full CAR [-5,+10] | forward CAR (t+1…+10) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **UST/Luna** (2022-05-09) | **−15.4%** | −5.1% |
| **USDC** (2023-03-11) | **+32.9%** | +29.1% |
| **Mean (n = 2)** | **+8.7%** | +12.0% |

- The thesis — "a depeg is a crypto-wide *sell* signal" — is **true for one event and
  flatly contradicted by the other.** UST's algorithmic collapse *was* a market-wide crash
  (basket −15.4%). But USDC depegged because Silicon Valley Bank failed, and the resulting
  banking panic was read as *bullish* for crypto (a flight from the banking system): the
  basket **rallied +32.9%** in the same window.
- The **mean CAR across the two events is +8.7% — positive**, the wrong sign for a "sell
  signal," and indistinguishable from an ordinary window (see the synthetic control).

## Why no t-stat — the n = 2 wall

| | Mean full CAR | HAC *t* | bootstrap CI | p (vs synthetic control) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Event study (n = 2) | +8.7% | **undefined** | [−15.4%, +32.9%] | **0.78** |
| Forward CAR (n = 2) | +12.0% | undefined | [−5.1%, +29.1%] | 0.88 |

- The universe of undisputed market-wide depegs is **n = 2**. A HAC/Newey-West *t* is
  **not even computable** off two observations (and a two-point CI just spans the two
  values) — so the real tape **cannot** clear the *t* ≥ 2 bar, by construction. Per the
  desk's inference bar, that alone forecloses a `REAL` stamp.
- The **synthetic control settles it anyway:** randomly-placed non-event windows produce a
  mean CAR at least as low as the observed +8.7% **78% of the time**. The two depeg
  windows are not unusual. "Depeg = sell" is indistinguishable from "pick two random weeks."

## Including the near-misses (n = 4) — still nothing

Adding the two near-misses we deliberately excluded from the headline (USDT's Oct-2022
wobble and the FTX-week USDT scare) gives **n = 4**: mean full CAR **+5.6%**, HAC
*t* = **+0.64**, p = 0.69. Even four events produce a positive mean and a *t* far below the
bar — there is no abnormal-return signal here.

## Could you trade it? — selling on the depeg LOSES money

The tradable rule: stay long the basket, but go to **cash** for 10 days after each depeg
(one documented execution lag — act at the close of day t+1, since the depeg is only
confirmed intraday on day t; costs one-way × NAV on each switch):

| round-trip cost | rule Sharpe | B&H Sharpe | cum. excess vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +1.00 | +1.00 | **−5.1%** |
| 10 bps | +1.00 | +1.00 | −5.5% |
| 30 bps | +1.00 | +1.00 | −6.3% |

Sitting out the post-depeg window **costs** you (−5.1% gross over the two events), because
the one window you most wanted to be in — the USDC rebound — is exactly the one the rule
makes you miss. Costs only deepen the hole. There is no edge to charge costs against; the
rule is a `MIRAGE` before the first basis point.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is a faithful detector

The same engine, run on a deterministic synthetic tape with a *planted* depeg crash,
recovers it cleanly (and reads ~null when nothing is planted) — so the real-tape "nothing"
is a statement about the **market**, not a broken harness:

| Planted shock | mean CAR | HAC *t* | p (vs null) | recovered? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (null) | +2.2% | +0.60 | 0.82 | no (correctly) |
| −0.05 | −7.7% | −2.36 | 0.06 | yes |
| −0.10 | −16.9% | −5.71 | 0.00 | yes |
| −0.20 | −33.5% | −13.82 | 0.00 | yes |

*(Note: the synthetic control plants 10 events so the machinery proof has the sample size
to clear the bar — the real tape's two events never will. A synthetic Sharpe/t never backs
a Signal stamp; it only proves the detector works.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The two real depegs point in **opposite directions** (UST −15.4%,
  USDC +32.9%); the mean CAR is *positive* (+8.7%, wrong sign), the synthetic control puts
  it at p = 0.78 (an utterly ordinary window), and with n = 2 no HAC *t* is even definable.
  The positive control confirms the engine would catch a real signal — there isn't one.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Selling on the depeg *underperforms* buy-and-hold by −5.1%
  before costs, because it forces you out of the USDC-week rebound. No edge exists to
  survive costs.
- **"Depeg = crypto-wide sell signal"? — BUSTED.** A depeg is a *symptom* whose market
  meaning depends entirely on *why* the coin broke: an endogenous crypto-native collapse
  (UST) drags the market down; an exogenous TradFi shock (USDC/SVB) can send it *up*. One
  bit — "a stablecoin lost its peg" — carries no directional information for the basket.
